inputs_detail.derivation: Aggregator consensus snippet ~$29.99 (single source, per supervisor) cross-checked bottom-up: organic ARR growth ~8-9% (Q3 ARR $27.50B +11.2% incl. ~$480M Semrush; FY guide 10.2% on $25.66B implies ~8.3% organic) plus ~6-7% annual share shrink from ~$2.2B/quarter buybacks, with ~45% non-GAAP op margin held and 18% tax rate; I keep ~11% EPS growth.

Adobe's fiscal year ends late November (Q3 ended Aug 28, 2026), so NTM from 2027-09-30 is ~2 months of FY27 and ~10 of FY28: 2/12 x $27.67 + 10/12 x $30.0 = $29.6; trimmed to ~$29.4 for reset risk at the first FY27 guide under a new CEO, interim CFO and without the Creative business president.

Stock trades ~8.8x NTM EPS (~$27) and ~9.7x FY26 guide; I allow a modest re-rating to 9.5x for a ~10%+ EPS grower with ~9% after-SBC FCF yield and falling share count, but not a return to historical 25x+ given organic net new ARR down ~36-37% y/y in Q3 and leadership turnover. Analyst average target ~$278-283 implies ~9.5-10x on this EPS base.

389.2M outstanding at Sept 18, 2026 (10-Q cover); Q4 diluted guide 389M; ~$2.2B/quarter buyback retires ~8.5M gross, ~7M net of issuance per quarter, giving ~362M by Sept 2027.
Debt $1.60B current + $4.77B long-term vs $5.64B cash and short-term investments at Aug 28, 2026; immaterial to per-share value.

Today's after-SBC yield is ~9.1% (TTM ~$8.4B / ~$92.6B market cap). I require slightly more (9.25%) than today, i.e. no re-rating, plus a small premium for the management turnover (new CEO Dec 1, interim CFO, Creative business president gone Sept 27 per 8-K).

bear.story: The first FY27 guide under a new CEO, an interim CFO and without the Creative business head (Wadhwani left Sept 27) resets targets lower; freemium keeps cannibalising paid Creative conversion, organic ARR growth slides to ~5-6%, and AI compute dents margins; ~$26 NTM EPS valued at ~6.5x as an ex-growth, AI-disrupted seat business.

base.story: Q4 delivers the 10.2% ARR guide (implied net new ARR ~$0.78B, ~-16% y/y, a smaller decline than Q3's ~-37%); FY27 targets land near consensus (~$27.7 EPS, high-single-digit growth); buybacks cut shares to ~362M; the multiple stays ~9x on ~$29.4 NTM EPS.

bull.story: AI-first ARR and Firefly/Acrobat AI monetisation plus deferred Creative Cloud pricing actions re-accelerate net new ARR in FY27; Chakravarthy's agentic/CX story and a strong new Creative leader gain credibility; multiple recovers to ~12x on ~$30 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$178 (under the 52-week low of $190 and ~6.4x FY27 consensus EPS of $27.67, despite a ~9% after-SBC FCF yield and ~7% annual share shrink) the market would be pricing an actual decline in earnings power, e.g. a December FY27 guide implying low-single-digit organic ARR growth, negative net new ARR in a quarter, or a margin reset from AI costs, rather than just multiple compression. The leadership gap (new CEO, interim CFO, Creative president gone) raises the odds of such a reset but does not by itself move the level.

reasoning: Primary documents show a business still compounding EPS double digits but with decelerating organic bookings. Q3 FY26 (8-K/10-Q): revenue $6.76B +13%, non-GAAP EPS $6.13 +15%, ARR $27.50B +11.2%; FY guide $24.45-24.50 EPS with ARR growth held at 10.2% on a $25.66B beginning book. Semrush (~$480M ARR) was in both Q2 and Q3 ending ARR, so the ~36-37% y/y Q3 net new ARR decline is essentially organic; the FY guide implies Q4 net new ARR ~$0.78B vs ~$0.93B a year earlier (~-16%), which is the December test. Round 2 changes after the supervisor review: (1) NTM EPS reweighted for Adobe's late-November fiscal year (2/12 FY27 + 10/12 FY28 = ~$29.6, trimmed to $29.4), lowering the P/E leg from $290 to $279; (2) FCF leg rebuilt from TTM CFO $10.81B with capex ~$0.25B, SBC deducted and ~362M shares, at 9.25% (today ~9.1%) = $274; (3) I verified in the Sept 8 8-K that David Wadhwani, President of Creativity & Productivity, stepped down effective Sept 27, 2026, which with a Dec 1 CEO change and an interim CFO raises reset risk at the ~Dec 9 FY27 guide, so I moved 2 points of probability to the bear case and trimmed the base price. Fair value falls from $281 to $277, close to the supervisor's $272 but I keep a slightly higher P/E multiple (9.5x vs 9.25x) because consensus targets and the ~10% EPS growth plus ~7% share shrink justify modest re-rating over 12 months. Scenario mean ~$260; I set the 12-month median ~$250 (P(>=spot) 0.555), below fair value because sentiment and the bookings trend argue for only partial convergence, with a ~36% lognormal-like width and a fat left tail for a guide reset. The 1-month ladder stays centred on spot since no Adobe event falls in the window. Research was limited (one follow-up fetch of the 8-K); FY28 consensus rests on a single aggregator snippet.
